summary: Recent changes to Firefox's WebRender, the GPU compositor that enhances how web pages are visually rendered, focus on improving performance and visual fidelity. Significant updates include the ability to _apply non-axis-aligned transforms_ to text and images, which means more dynamic and visually rich designs can be implemented without sacrificing quality. Additionally, several legacy image processing paths have been removed, streamlining the rendering process and making it more efficient. This work culminates in smoother animations and transitions, delivering a **more responsive browsing experience** for users when interacting with web content.
